Restaurant unit growth may be constrained by availability and cost of franchisee financing, sale-leaseback proceeds, development lines, rent coverage, and remodel capex rather than consumer demand alone.

node: Franchisee financing, remodel capex, sale-leaseback, small-box restaurant real estate, and development services
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the restaurant theme into the less obvious capital-enablement layer: net-lease landlords, sale-leaseback REITs, and franchise lenders that may determine whether franchise-heavy restaurant systems can keep opening and remodeling units. The strongest direct mappings found are restaurant-heavy net-lease REIT FCPT and franchise/SBA lenders LOB and WTFC. EPRT is a broader middle-market sale-leaseback platform with QSR exposure but requires verification of restaurant rent mix. These are second-order beneficiaries rather than restaurant demand owners; the key chokepoint test is whether higher rates, rent coverage, construction costs, or franchisee credit quality begin to constrain brand-level unit targets.
